title: No shame in ignorance where Scripture is silent: it teaches that God rules all, not the mode
source_text: XLIX. Nec me pudet hujus meae ignorantiae. Tuto enim ignoratur, quod nec Deus aperte in verbo suo revelavit, nec humana ratio per se investigare potest. Jam autem scriptura sacra manifeste docet quidem, omnia divina providentia regi, nec quicquam, nisi ipso consulto sinente, fieri, & ab aeterno Deo nota esse & definita omnia opera sua: modum vero quo Deus causas secundas movet, quae sit ratio decretorum illius, & qua ratione illa exequatur, & omnia ad finem destinatum perducat, scriptura sacra non aperit, nec studet humanae curiositati super eo satisfacere.
pass_a_gloss: XLIX. Nor am I ashamed of this my ignorance. For that is safely not known, which neither God has openly revealed in his word, nor human reason can investigate by itself. But now sacred scripture plainly teaches indeed, that all things are ruled by divine providence, and that nothing is done, except he advisedly allowing it, and that from eternity all his works are known and defined to God: but the mode by which God moves second causes, what is the nature of his decrees, and in what way he executes them, and leads all things to the destined end, sacred scripture does not open, nor is it eager to satisfy human curiosity about it.
pass_b_english: I am not ashamed of this ignorance of mine. It is safe not to know what God has not openly revealed in his word and what human reason cannot search out by itself.

Holy Scripture does plainly teach that all things are governed by divine providence, that nothing happens unless he deliberately allows it, and that all his works are known to God and settled from eternity.

But how God moves second causes, what the nature of his decrees is, how he carries them out and brings all things to their appointed end, Holy Scripture does not disclose, nor does it seek to satisfy human curiosity on the point.
